channel.title: World News

item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro posts video, says he fled Brazil due to ‘persecution’
item.description: Brazil's defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro posted a video message on social media late Friday to declare he fled to the US because he was a victim of 'persecution'. Bolsonaro, who lost Sunday's election runoff to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, gave no details of how he left the country.

item.title: Live: France braces for Halloween protests, government vows tough response
item.description: France on Saturday braced for a third weekend of protests coinciding with Halloween, with authorities alert to the possibility that rioters could use festive masks to conceal their identities. Around 70,000 security personnel have been deployed to prevent a repeat of street violence that erupted two weeks ago. Follow our live blog for all the latest updates.

item.title: WATCH: Runner looks forward to his 50th straight NYC marathon
item.description: ABC News’ Linsey Davis speaks to 83-year-old Dave Obelkevich ahead of his record 50th straight NYC marathon race and why it’s a tradition for him and his family.

item.title: Burnham 'open' to slavery apology - as King continues Caribbean tour
item.description: Andy Burnham has said he is "open" to calls for Britain to make a formal apology for its role in the slave trade as the King continues his tour of the Caribbean.

item.description: Riot police were deployed to Poland's Constitutional Tribunal on Friday as hundreds of demonstrators gathered to protest against the suspension of the top court's president by the current pro-European government.

item.title: Selma Blair apologizes in video weeks after arrest: 'I take this very seriously'
item.description: Selma Blair is speaking out weeks after her arrest.

item.title: Halloween Protests & French Promises, US Mid Term Mood, What now for Israel?
item.description: France braces for another weekend of unrest as the Yellow Vests return to the streets under the rallying cry of ‘Act III – Halloween’, with 70,000 police and security forces deployed after the riots and looting of recent weeks. A cash-strapped government faces mounting grievances, a rolling protest movement and little room for manoeuvre ahead of elections, as it struggles to restore order while grappling with crippling debt.

item.title: Peltola denies knowing of 'any other candidate' on ballot besides herself, incumbent
item.description: The DOJ is acting to "intensely and swiftly" escalate its probe, the top federal prosecutor in Alaska said.

item.title: Ebola outbreak kills more than 5,000 people in Democratic Republic of Congo
item.description: More than 5,000 people have now died from an Ebola outbreak in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), according to government data.

item.title: Despite concerns, the Trump administration still sends pregnant migrant minors to south Texas
item.description: Several children have had to leave the state to receive medical care, including abortions, that is unavailable in Texas.

item.title: Judge orders an inquiry into potential DOJ misconduct in Trump's golf course case
item.description: A federal judge is opening an formal inquiry into Trump officials' conduct in the East Potomac case, including whether they misled the court about their plans for the municipal golf course.

item.title: First Youth Olympic Games in Africa
item.description: In tonight's show, the Senegalese capital is hosting the first Olympic event ever held in Africa, welcoming nearly 2,700 athletes for the 2026 Youth Olympic Games. Also, South Africa’s local elections are set for November 4, with the African National Congress facing growing pressure over its record in local government. And finally we are joined by Muse L'Artiste who's reconnecting to her roots with her latest EP Heritage bringing her father's compositions back to life.

item.title: Residents leave Russian-occupied Oleshky in evacuation operation
item.description: Residents evacuated from the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky have left for Russia's Anapa city with a Ukrainian delegation, senior official David Arakhamia said Friday. They are expected to fly to Belarus before returning to Ukraine by bus, during a rare ceasefire brokered by the United States.

item.title: These House races could determine which party is in control in the next Congress
item.description: All 435 seats in the House of Representatives are on the ballot when voters head to the polls on Nov. 3.

item.title: WATCH: How to keep pets safe on Halloween
item.description: Experts say some candy can contain ingredients that owners may not know are dangerous. Dr. Gary Richter, veterinarian and founder of "Ultimate Pet Nutrition," shares more pet safety tips.

item.title: UN nature summit approves two key agreements after marathon negotiations
item.description: Almost 200 nations approved two agreements on Friday to halt biodiversity loss by 2030, following almost two weeks of negotiations that ran into extra time on the final day.

item.title: Voters weigh citizenship amendments as Trump fans fears of noncitizen election fraud
item.description: Civil rights groups warn millions of Americans could get sidelined.

item.title: 'Five churches set on fire by Muslims?' Fake news by Islamophobic social media accounts
item.description: Several social media accounts associated with sharing anti-immigrant views claim French Muslims were responsible for burning five churches on October 17 – the day the nation was rocked by en masse protests. But both this number and story are fictitious. The French government agency that monitors religious heritage sites confirmed only one fire in a church occured in recent days; its cause unknown.

item.title: WATCH: Baby loons play with their moms in must-see video
item.description: You can see more about the baby loons and other animals on "Inside the Enchanted Waterways" on Disney+.

item.title: MAGA: Why Trump's movement is fracturing?
item.description: As the 2026 midterm elections approach, divisions within the MAGA camp are becoming increasingly visible. From the war in Iran and rising fuel prices to the Epstein files, several of Trump’s decisions are fuelling divisions among his most loyal supporters. Once united by a shared vision of America, MAGA now brings together factions that increasingly disagree over foreign policy, the economy and what “America First” should actually mean. Yet Trump remains the central figure holding this political coalition together – and he is fighting to keep it that way. Why are some of the president’s longtime allies distancing themselves from him? Can MAGA remain united despite these disagreements? And can Trump still mobilise his base ahead of the midterms? 🔍 Our journalist Stella Elgersma breaks down the divisions within the MAGA movement and Donald Trump’s strategy to rally his supporters, once again.

item.title: G20 photocall axed after Miliband and other ministers refuse to be pictured with top Russian diplomat
item.description: A photocall of foreign ministers was cancelled by the US after the UK's Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband and other European counterparts refused to be pictured with Russia's envoy Sergei Lavrov.

item.title: ICE activity is surging ahead of midterms. So is voter turnout.
item.description: Across the country, there are reports of heightened ICE activity. Advocates worry about how close it is to midterms, but so far voter turnout is surging.

item.title: Motorist who dragged cyclist under his car for more than a mile guilty of murder
item.description: A motorist has been found guilty of murder after hitting a cyclist and knowingly dragging him for more than a mile under his car.

item.title: Oleshky: No access to basic needs, ceasefire offers limited opportunity for humanitarian assistance
item.description: Catherine Viette is pleased to welcome Jens Schumacher, Field Coordinator in Mykolaiv and Kherson with Solidarity International. Just a few kilometers separate the Ukrainian-controlled city of Kherson from Russian-occupied Oleshky. For civilians caught between military occupation, disrupted essential services and uncertain evacuation arrangements, geographical proximity offers little guarantee of access to life-saving assistance. Schumacher examines the humanitarian implications of a temporary ceasefire around Oleshky, where approximately 2,000 civilians were reported to remain. Although the cessation of attacks has created a limited opportunity for humanitarian operations, the geographical scope of the agreement, the prospects for evacuation and the possibility of sustained humanitarian access remain uncertain.

item.title: Russia’s Novaya Gazeta to cease publication amid Kremlin crackdown
item.description: Russia’s most renowned independent newspaper, Novaya Gazeta, announced on Friday that it was ceasing publication after more than three decades. Known for its courageous investigative journalism, the flagship newspaper said the Kremlin’s crackdown and ban on the media outlet had made it impossible to continue its work.

item.title: 'The International Criminal Court deserves the Sakharov Prize': CJEU President Koen Lenaerts
item.description: We speak to the influential and long-serving president of the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU), Koen Lenaerts. The court is the EU's supreme judicial authority, responsible for ensuring that European law is interpreted and applied across all 27 member states.

item.title: Stranded locals use rare truce to leave Moscow-occupied town in Ukraine
item.description: Some residents of Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town in southern Ukraine ravaged by food and medicine shortages, left on Friday during a rare ceasefire brokered by the United States – due to end on Sunday evening. Ukrainian and Russian officials visited the town together on Friday, delivering aid and marshalling those who wanted to leave.

item.title: WATCH: What we know about Binance security breach
item.description: Dave Merkel, co-founder and CEO of cybersecurity company Expel, talks about the major breach.

item.title: Star Wars: Has Russia's war with Ukraine gone intergalactic?
item.description: Russian made an unprecedented combative move this month as one of its military satellites, the Cosmos-2612, encroached upon the orbit of Ukrainian commercial satellite, Iceye-X36, in behaviour deemed "threatening" by the US State Department. Norbert Pouzin, an orbital analyst at French space tech firm, Aldoria, described the mercenary manoeuvre as the first of its kind.

item.title: Could US midterms impact the EU? Transatlantic ties hit new low after Trump-Putin diesel deal
item.description: From the EU's perspective, the second Trump presidency has felt even more destabilising than the first. From making the false claim that the EU was set up to "screw" the United States, to slapping tariffs on European goods, to making territorial claims on Greenland, to doing a diesel deal with Vladimir Putin and telling Ukraine to get a new president, Donald Trump has more than ruffled feathers on this side of the ocean. He has shaken the very foundations of the historical transatlantic relationship.

item.title: French port strikes: Unions 'will get better working conditions', but can they curb militarisation?
item.description: Carys Garland is pleased to welcome Renaud Foucart, Senior Lecturer at the Department of Economics ECARES at Lancaster University. An international dockworkers’ strike brings into focus the relationship between organized labor, technological change and Europe’s expanding military investment. Foucart argues that port workers’ strategic position in global supply chains gives them exceptional leverage: “They know how powerful they are.” While questioning their ability to redirect military policy, he expects that leverage to secure concessions on automation and working conditions: “They can get those concessions. And I think they will get them.”

item.title: War in Ukraine: Evacuations under way in Russian-occupied Oleshky
item.description: Starving and exhausted residents of Oleshky, a Russian-occupied town in southern Ukraine, were being evacuated on Friday, October 30, as part of a joint relief operation involving the opposing sides – the first operation of its kind in four years and eight months of war. FRANCE 24’s Ukraine correspondent Emmanuelle Chaze reports.

item.title: French crowd gathers for anti-islamophobia rally in Paris suburb after attack
item.description: In France, thousands were protesting in the Paris suburb of La Verrière on Friday, a week after a racist terrorist attack killed one person and injured five others. The suspect, identified as Kevin T., admitted he was targeting people based on their appearance or religion and has been transferred to a Paris court. FRANCE 24's Morgan Ayre reports.

item.title: WATCH: State of the race with 4 days until midterm vote
item.description: Nearly 45 million people have already turned out to vote, and those early voting numbers have surpassed where the numbers were at this point in the 2022 midterm election.

item.title: Biggest hack in history: Cryptocurrency giant Binance loses $6.3 billion
item.description: Cryptocurrency exchange giant Binance has been targeted by a record-breaking $6.3 billion cyber heist, with blockchain intelligence firms linking the attack to North Korea. By Thursday night in the US, a coordinated effort by major crypto platforms successfully froze roughly $3 billion of the stolen assets during a high-stakes race to track and secure the digital funds.

item.title: Spain working to identify train crash dead as relatives' anguish grows
item.description: A second day of mourning is underway in Spain, with some families still waiting for news about missing loved ones, following Wednesday's high speed train crash that killed 69 people. Some have flooded social media with desperate appeals for information, posting photos or describing the clothes their relatives were wearing when they boarded the trains.

item.title: Midterms 2026: The former neo-Nazi pastor speaking out against Trump
item.description: According to one poll, 82 per cent of white evangelical Protestants voted for Donald Trump in the 2024 US presidential election. That makes pastor Caleb Campbell a significant outlier – he has been one of the few outspoken evangelical critics of the Trump administration, dating back to the president’s first term when he felt compelled to speak out against Trump’s plans to put “kids in cages” as part of an immigration crackdown. “I was told that I was possessed by a demon,” Campbell remembers. Now, as the midterms approach, he fears US politics and the current administration have become more distant than ever from the Bible’s teachings.

item.title: Israeli election: 'Netanyahu did not win, he lost dramatically,' former PM Barak says
item.description: In an interview with FRANCE 24, former Israeli prime minister Ehud Barak said Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu "did not win" this week's election in Israel but "lost dramatically", and that his rival Gadi Eisenkot should ally with Arab parties. Barak also suggested that claims of Qatari funding for an Arab party aimed to distract from an ongoing corruption scandal, and warned that Netanyahu was ready to strike Iran to stay in power.

item.title: 'Deeply hurt': Convicted murderer Christa Pike speaks out after botched execution
item.description: Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike said she remains in constant pain after surviving a botched lethal injection in September, in her first public statement since the failed execution. She expressed gratitude for those who saved her life while urging compassion for her victim's family.

item.title: Israel's election ends in deadlock as final results show no clear winner
item.description: Israel's wartime election appeared deadlocked on Tuesday, exit polls showed, ​with Gadi Eisenkot's opposition bloc running neck and neck with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's camp, leaving neither side with a clear path to power. The projections pointed to a setback for Netanyahu's coalition and potentially weeks of political wrangling to form a government. FRANCE 24's Jerusalem correspondent Noga Tarnopolsky has more.

item.title: NPR special: 5 takeaways from a year of listening to swing voters
item.description: Every election, there is a crucial sliver of voters who help determine which candidates win. Here are five takeaways from a year of listening to voters who backed Biden in 2020 and then Trump in 2024.

item.title: Bugatti CEO chases down car thief - then offers him lift home
item.description: The head of the luxury car-maker Bugatti has promised to stop leaving his keys in his own car after his £2m model was stolen from a company site in Zagreb.

item.title: France braces for new wave of protests, govt warns of 'very high' violence risk
item.description: France's interior minister on Thursday warned of a "very high risk of public disorder" and announced the deployment of around 70,000 police officers for a new wave of protests this weekend. France has been rocked by widespread anger over the rising cost of living and inequality, with nationwide demonstrations on October 17 degenerating into some of the country's worst rioting in years. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Rochelle Ferguson Bouyahi tells us more.

item.description: Rep. Huffman wants "guardrails" to keep the president from profiting from it.

item.description: The DOJ is issuing new subpoenas in a probe of Alaska's U.S. Senate race and alleged efforts by Democrats to recruit a candidate with the same name as the GOP incumbent.
